About O.U.H.D.

A Global Humanitarian Mandate, Rooted in Ecuador.

Originally established in April 2022 as Fundación Lafior EC (Resolution MIES-CZ-4-2022-0025-R) and formally restated in 2026 as Organización Universal Humanitaria de Desarrollo (O.U.H.D.), our institution operates under Ecuadorian civil law with the authority to establish national and international offices.

Per Articles 2 and 6 of our certified statutes, O.U.H.D. designs and executes programmes for economic and social inclusion across the entire life cycle—prioritizing girls, boys, adolescents, youth, older adults, persons with disabilities, and communities facing poverty or disaster.

Early childhood & community inclusion initiatives aligned with Statute Art. 7(d) & Treaty Art. 3.

Our Vision

A just, resilient, and inclusive global society where every individual—from early childhood to older adulthood—exercises full human rights, social mobility, and sustainable livelihoods free from hunger and exclusion.

Our Mission

To formulate and execute transparent humanitarian relief, educational, healthcare, and solidarity-economy programmes in partnership with governments, UN-accredited bodies, and civil society across Latin America, Africa, and MENA.

Core Values

  • Human Dignity & Non-Discrimination
  • Audited Financial Transparency
  • Solidarity Economy & Self-Sufficiency
  • Diplomatic & Multilateral Cooperation

Institutional Timeline

  • Apr 2022: Legal incorporation in Manabí, Ecuador (MIES-CZ-4-2022-0025-R).
  • Jun–Oct 2026: Statutory restatement as O.U.H.D. (MTDH-DPMAN-2026-0007-R).
  • Nov 2026: 5-Year Strategic Partnership Treaty signed with Morocco UN-DESA partner.
Statutory Governance (Art. 23 & Art. 35)

Executive Leadership & Councils

Governed by the General Assembly and an elected Executive Board serving two-year renewable mandates under Ecuadorian law, supported by an International Advisory Council and Regional Directors.

President · Executive Board

Oscar Larry Ulloa del Hierro

Legal and judicial representative of O.U.H.D. (Statute Art. 42). Presides over the General Assembly, Executive Board, and institutional treasury oversight.

Secretary-General & Authorized Signatory

H.E. Counselor Dr. Mohamed Farouk

Authorized diplomatic signatory (Official Letter MTDH-DPMAN-2026-0169-OF). Leads international treaties, ECOSOC consultative coordination, and MENA/Africa affairs.

Executive Board (La Directiva)

Vice President & Treasurer

Statutory officers elected by the General Assembly (Art. 35, 44, 46) responsible for annual budgets, quarterly financial audits, and asset stewardship.

Advisory & Regional Commissions

Advisory Council & Directors

Permanent and special commissions (Art. 47) overseeing education, health, human rights, internal fiscal control, and Latin America–Africa corridors.

Diplomatic Treaties & Official Dispatches

Press Release · Nov 12, 2026 · Bilateral Treaty

O.U.H.D. and Morocco Human Rights Center Ratify 5-Year Strategic Partnership Treaty

Signed by Secretary-General H.E. Counselor Dr. Mohamed Farouk and President Bousselham El Hamdaoui (UN DESA NGO Branch Profile ID: 699741), the binding 9-article treaty establishes joint emergency funds for SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), early childhood centers, elderly & disability healthcare, and audited financial governance across Latin America and Africa.

Financial Accountability

Transparent Resource Governance

Per Statute Articles 48–50 and Strategic Treaty Article 7, all donations, grants, and member contributions are subject to international accounting standards, quarterly board reviews, and annual external audits closing December 31.
